children.translated_text: <s>Oṃ</s>, homage to <s>Cidbhairava</s> (Consciousness-<s>Bhairava</s>)!

children.text: citibhūmisamāśrayaṇāś citibhūtiṃ śrayata mā mudhā bhramata |
children.translated_text: 'Take refuge in the ground of consciousness (<s>citibhūmi</s>), resort to the glory of consciousness (<s>citibhūti</s>), do not wander in vain!' —
Proclaiming thus to the devoted, victorious is <s>Śiva</s>, inclined toward grace (<s>anugraha</s>).

children.text: cidbhairavam eva paraṃ paramāmṛtarūpam ekam atidīptam |
children.translated_text: I worship <s>Cidbhairava</s> alone, the supreme, of the form of supreme nectar (<s>paramāmṛta</s>), one, exceedingly radiant,
who has swallowed the entirety [of the universe] through the outflashing circle of [cognitive] organs (<s>karaṇacakra</s>) — <s>Śiva</s>.

children.text: stutyaḥ stotā stutir iti yad api vibhinnaṃ na kiṃcid astīha |
children.translated_text: Although the praised (<s>stutya</s>), the praiser (<s>stotā</s>), and the praise (<s>stuti</s>) — here nothing is truly different;

children.text: mṛṣati yathā yad rūpaṃ cidrūpatayā tathā bhavaty etat ||
children.translated_text: whatever form appears falsely, by virtue of being of the nature of consciousness (<s>cidrūpatā</s>), this [distinction] also becomes [consciousness].
Your reality (<s>tattva</s>), O Lord, in which all distinctions have dissolved yet which is of the nature of all distinctions, a solid mass of consciousness and bliss (<s>cidghanānanda</s>) —

children.text: yat tava tattvaṃ bhagavaṃs tasyānukṛtiṃ tvadākṛtiṃ vande ||
children.translated_text: I worship the imitation (<s>anukṛti</s>) of that, your form (<s>ākṛti</s>).
Just as a line-drawing reveals a person, and written letters reveal a collection of sounds,

children.text: tadvat vicitrarūpaṃ tvām ākāro vyanakti paramātman ||
children.translated_text: so too, O Supreme Self (<s>Paramātman</s>), a form (<s>ākāra</s>) reveals you of variegated form.
There, entering you who are beyond conceptual construction (<s>avikalpa</s>), of the nature of consciousness (<s>cidrūpa</s>),

children.text: vimṛśāmaḥ kim api manāṅ na hi tattvaṃ kalpanāviṣayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: we contemplate somewhat — for the reality is not the domain of conceptual construction (<s>kalpanā</s>).
Having established as self-radiant the goddess of speech (<s>Vāgdevī</s>), worshipped with offerings of sense-object flowers,

children.text: prathamonmeṣaṃ gurum atha vanditvā hṛdayam āviśya ||
children.translated_text: then having saluted the <s>guru</s> of the first awakening (<s>prathamonmeṣa</s>), having entered the heart —

children.text: staumi vimṛśan maheśvaram ātmānaṃ svaṃ cidekaghanam |
children.translated_text: I praise, reflecting upon (<s>vimṛśan</s>), the great Lord (<s>Maheśvara</s>), the Self, one's own [Self], a solid mass of consciousness alone (<s>cidekaghanam</s>),
who has caused the multitude of bonds (<s>pāśakadambaka</s>) to flow away, in this body-temple (<s>dehadevagṛha</s>).

O all-pervading one (<s>vibhu</s>), your powers (<s>śaktis</s>) called consciousness (<s>cit</s>), bliss (<s>ānanda</s>), will (<s>icchā</s>), knowledge (<s>vit</s>), and action (<s>karaṇa</s>) are victorious,
attaining the distinction of subtle and gross, they become the faces (<s>vaktras</s>) called <s>Brahma</s>, <s>Muṇḍa</s>, and so forth.
The group of six limbs (<s>aṅgaṣaṭka</s>) beginning with the heart (<s>hṛdaya</s>), whose domain is omniscience (<s>sarvajñatā</s>) and the like — that is yours.
The entire [realm] up to <s>Sadāśiva</s>, as having the nature of a corpse (<s>pretātmatā</s>), is your seat (<s>āsana</s>), O Lord.
O Lord, of you whose body is supreme light (<s>paramaprakāśa</s>), the power of reflective awareness (<s>vimarśaśakti</s>) is the supreme Goddess (<s>Parā Devī</s>);

children.text: asyā eva prasaraḥ sarvā brāhmyādikā devyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: all the goddesses beginning with <s>Brāhmī</s> are an expansion (<s>prasara</s>) of her alone.
Bearing fire, water, nectar, the [crescent] moon-mark, poison, and the like, you teach this:

children.text: viśvaṃ viruddham api saccidrūpe mayi virudhyate naitat ||
children.translated_text: 'Even this contradictory (<s>viruddha</s>) universe, in me who am of the nature of being and consciousness (<s>saccidrūpa</s>), does not contradict.'
'This insubstantial host of perceivers (<s>mātṛnivaha</s>), dissolved in the thread of awareness (<s>saṃvitsūtra</s>) —'
'By bearing the garland of skulls (<s>muṇḍamālā</s>) of the organs (<s>karaṇa</s>), you show us thus, O Lord.'

children.text: paśyata paśyata pāśā viṣamās ta ime bahiṣkṛtāḥ śaśvat |
children.translated_text: 'See, see! These uneven bonds (<s>pāśas</s>) — they have been always cast outside!' —

children.text: ity antradhāraṇamiṣat kathayaṃs tvaṃ naḥ samābhāsi ||
children.translated_text: Under the pretext of bearing entrails (<s>antradhāraṇa</s>), saying thus, you shine forth to us.

children.text: māyāpaṭaḥ sarāgo vyomni pare 'smin sa eṣa nikṣiptaḥ |
children.translated_text: 'This veil (<s>paṭa</s>) of <s>Māyā</s>, tinged with passion (<s>sarāga</s>), has been cast off in this supreme sky (<s>vyoman</s>)' —

children.text: iti gajacarma saraktaṃ mūrdhni vahan kathayasīśa ||
children.translated_text: Thus, O Lord (<s>Īśa</s>), bearing the blood-stained elephant-skin upon your head, you declare.
You reveal by means of the sword (<s>asi</s>) the inner power-sword (<s>śaktikṛpāṇī</s>) that cuts through worldly existence (<s>saṃsṛti</s>);
for the supreme heroes (<s>vīravaras</s>), who have appropriated the entire universe through the greatness of their own power, [this is natural].
'I am that destroyer of the fear of existence (<s>bhavabhaya</s>); I stand in [your] protection — do not fear!' —
Thus, O Lord, by displaying the raised shield (<s>kheṭaka</s>), you bestow [assurance] upon us.
'Ensnared by the noose (<s>pāśa</s>) of my own power (<s>nijaśakti</s>), time (<s>kāla</s>) is fashioned by me through the body of consciousness (<s>cidvapus</s>)' —

children.text: iti pāśadhāraṇavaśāt prathayasi naḥ kālakālas tvam ||
children.translated_text: Thus, by the bearing of the noose, you manifest to us, O destroyer of time (<s>Kālakāla</s>)!
'I cast away all this [world] of differentiation (<s>bhedamaya</s>) by my own power alone, in order to reabsorb [it]' —
Thus, by the bearing of the goad (<s>aṅkuśa</s>), the supreme <s>Bhairava</s> makes clear to us.
By displaying the arrow mounted on the bow (<s>kodaṇḍa</s>), [you split] <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, <s>Rudra</s>, <s>Īśa</s>,

children.text: sasadākhyaśivāñ chaktyā kāraṇahariṇaṃ bhinatsi mṛgavat tvam ||
children.translated_text: <s>Sadākhya-Śiva</s> — you split the deer of causation (<s>kāraṇahariṇa</s>) like a [hunted] deer, by means of [your] power (<s>śakti</s>).
With the boon-granting hand (<s>varada</s>), you enact the bestowal of the sovereignty of the universe (<s>viśvavibhūti</s>);

children.text: na khalu paratattvaniṣṭho vibhavamalaiḥ spṛśyate jātu ||
children.translated_text: indeed, one established in the supreme reality (<s>paratattva</s>) is never touched by the stains of worldly prosperity (<s>vibhava</s>).

children.text: abhayena ca bhavabhayāni unmūlayatā prakāśyate satatam |
children.translated_text: And by the hand [granting] fearlessness (<s>abhaya</s>), which uproots the fears of existence (<s>bhavabhaya</s>), there is constantly manifested
your inherent nature as the cause of grace (<s>anugraha</s>) toward the entire universe, by your palm (<s>karatala</s>).
'This here is the severed head of <s>Māyā</s>, of the nature of non-manifestation (<s>akhyāti</s>), incomparable' —

children.text: parabodhamayena mayā muṇḍaṃ bibhrat prakāśayasy evam ||
children.translated_text: Bearing the skull (<s>muṇḍa</s>) thus, you who are pervaded by supreme awakening (<s>parabodha</s>) reveal [this truth].
'In me alone, the solid mass of consciousness (<s>cidekaghana</s>), rests the existence of the world, its essence entirely absorbed' —
Thus, under the pretext of carrying the skull-staff (<s>khaṭvāṅga</s>) and skeleton (<s>karaṅka</s>), you issue the command (<s>ājñā</s>).
Playing the <s>vīṇā</s>, bell (<s>ghaṇṭā</s>), and <s>ḍamaru</s>, and waving the fly-whisk (<s>uḍḍāmara</s>), you teach this:
'I stand hearing the sound (<s>nāda</s>) divided by the three modes (<s>vṛttitribheda</s>) [of cognition].'
Moreover, O God, the great power (<s>mahāśakti</s>), beautiful as the spoke of the triad of powers beginning with <s>Parā</s> —
You imitate [her] externally, under the pretext of always bearing the trident (<s>triśūla</s>).
The supreme power (<s>Parā Śakti</s>) of your own — which illuminates through the powers of will (<s>icchā</s>) and the rest the triad of lower domains [of experience] —

children.text: svām eva parāṃ śaktiṃ vajramayīṃ vahasi ṣaḍarāṃ tvam ||
children.translated_text: You bear as a six-spoked thunderbolt (<s>vajra</s>) of <s>ṣaḍara</s> (six spokes).

children.text: jagad akhilaṃ macchaktyā damitaṃ sarvavyāvasthitīr dhatte |
children.translated_text: 'The entire world, subdued by my power (<s>śakti</s>), assumes all states of being (<s>vyavasthitis</s>)' —
Thus, by the bearing of the staff (<s>daṇḍa</s>), O <s>Cidbhairava</s>, you reveal to us.
Bearing a mace and an axe, which are forms imitating the <s>Bindu</s> and <s>Nāda</s>,
you indicate, O <s>Īśāna</s>, your supremacy in splitting, piercing, and shattering [all duality].

children.text: darśanabhedāt svāminn anyānyām āhṛtiṃ dadhānas tvam |
children.translated_text: Assuming, O Lord, different modes of absorption according to the diversity of philosophical viewpoints,
you manifest everywhere your own abode, which consists of the supreme awakening of <s>Bhairava</s>.

children.text: śāktāṇḍakhaṇḍamadhye viśvarasāḥ sarvam ahaṃ pibāmi sadā |
children.translated_text: "In the midst of the sphere of the <s>Śākta</s> cosmic egg, I constantly drink all the essences of the universe"—
you reveal this [truth] within me, as if through [the symbolism of] the human skull-cup, blood, and flesh.
"These two [skulls] with their tufts represent the uprooting of the bonds of the ego-heart"—

children.text: mūrtāv iva muṇdābjau prathayan dhatse mahākālaḥ ||
children.translated_text: displaying them as though they were embodied severed heads and lotuses, you bear [them] as <s>Mahākāla</s>.
You imitate the primordial [<s>Śakti</s>], the womb of the seed of the entire universe, O treasury of consciousness,
through the playful display of showing a <s>bījapūraka</s> (citron) in the palm of your hand, O Lord.

children.text: bhairavarūpo 'py asi yat tatrāpi kare 'kṣamālikāṃ dhatse |
children.translated_text: Though you are of <s>Bhairava</s>-form, the fact that you bear a rosary (<s>akṣamālā</s>) in your hand even there—
that [signifies that] through the blossoming of all the senses (<s>akṣa</s>), you revolve the universe within [yourself].
Adorned with bones, skulls, garlands of severed heads, and ashes, delighting in human blood—
you, O Lord, thus proclaim that the universe, being made of <s>Brahman</s>, is pure.

children.text: svātmārāmamayānāṃ viṣamā api viṣayabudbudhāḥ kim amī |
children.translated_text: "For those who delight in the Self (<s>svātmārāma</s>), what [harm] are even these turbulent bubbles of sense-objects?"—
displaying the burning of <s>Smara</s> (the Love-god) [and] the third eye on the forehead, you teach [us] the form of the supreme fire.
The fact that you always remain with your gaze fixed inwardly, even though your senses are fully expanded—
thereby you manifest the Self in all states, free from the stain of delusion.

children.text: deva digambaratā te vadati nirāvaraṇam ātmano rūpam |
children.translated_text: O Lord, your nakedness (<s>digambaratā</s>) proclaims the uncovered nature of the Self;
how could the veil of <s>Māyā</s> cover [you who are] the sun composed of the supreme <s>Brahman</s>?
"I am the destroyer of all [luminaries] beginning with the sun, I am the ground of darkness"—
this you demonstrate by [your] body, which has the radiance of the clear autumn sky.
O Lord, you who are made of the supreme <s>Brahman</s>, when you assume the form of <s>Bhairava</s>,

children.text: tat prathayasi tattvajñaḥ saty api bhede vimukta iti ||
children.translated_text: thereby you proclaim: "One who knows reality (<s>tattvajña</s>) is liberated even in the midst of duality."
Surrounded by garlands of various cremation-grounds and <s>vetālas</s> (vampiric spirits), you make manifest:
"Amidst the manifold calculations of the objects of consciousness, I am <s>Citi-Bhairava</s> (Consciousness-Bhairava)."
The crescent of nectar (<s>amṛtalekhā</s>) upon you, made of the supreme <s>Śakti</s>—[it shows that you are] the supreme Subject (<s>parapramātṛ</s>);

children.text: nātha tvam eva jagatām jīvanam iti bhāsi no hṛdaye ||
children.translated_text: therefore, O Lord, you alone are the life of the worlds—thus you shine in our hearts.
Of you whose body is the aggregate of sounds (<s>śabdarāśi</s>), the external retinue in each group of eight
consists of the <s>Lokeśvaras</s> (Lords of the Worlds) and others, O <s>Bhairava</s>, differentiated as <s>Para</s>, <s>Sūkṣma</s>, and so forth.
Your <s>mudrā</s> (seal-gesture) seals (<s>mudrayati</s>) all this, through the complete transference [of everything] into one's own nature;
it delights (<s>modayati</s>) the host of devotees, granting the bliss of [liberated] movement through the manifestation of fullness (<s>pūrṇatā</s>);

children.text: mocayati pāśajālaṃ drāvayati vibhedam īśa te mūrtiḥ |
children.translated_text: it liberates (<s>mocayati</s>) the net of bonds, and it dissolves (<s>drāvayati</s>) duality, O Lord—your form [does all this];
it seals (<s>mudrayati</s>) the wealth of manifold consciousness—therefore it is called <s>mudrā</s>.
this [<s>Bhairava</s>] who has become the very source [of all]
Victorious on the supreme ground of the highest reality,
may he clearly dwell [in us], dispelling the impurity of the knowable (<s>meya-mala</s>) from the heart through the manifestation of true reality.

children.text: pratikalam udeti saṃvid yā kila tatra sphuraty adho viśvam |
children.translated_text: The consciousness that arises at every moment—and within which the universe flashes forth below—
those who abide in worship (<s>yāga</s>), O <s>Maheśa</s>, know [this] as the form of the glory of <s>Śiva</s> and <s>Śakti</s>.

children.text: itthaṃ sphurasi sadā me cidbhairava sarvabhūtātma |
children.translated_text: Thus you always flash forth within me, O <s>Cid-Bhairava</s> (Consciousness-Bhairava), Self of all beings;
therefore, everything from worship (<s>yāga</s>) to recitation (<s>japa</s>) has been effortlessly accomplished.
Thus ends the <s>Bhairavānukaraṇastotra</s> (Hymn of Imitation of <s>Bhairava</s>) composed by the revered great <s>Māheśvara</s> teacher, the glorious <s>Kṣemarāja</s>.
